answer: Verifiable delay functions resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve sequential, non-parallelizable puzzles before registering at an interaction wharf. To flood a service meadow with fake peers, an attacker must allocate dedicated single-core runtime for each identity, preventing a dense dune of virtual processes from sharing compute. However, adversaries deploying customized low-latency ASICs can generate these proofs faster than commodity hardware.
